article_title: Blood Transfusion Knowledge among Nurses in Malaysia: A University Hospital Experience.
citation: Mohd Noor Noor Haslina, Saad Noor Hafiza, Khan Mohammad, Hassan Mohd Nazri, Ramli Marini, Bahar Rosnah, Mohamed Yusoff Shafini, Iberahim Salfarina, Wan Ab Rahman Wan Suriana, Zulkafli Zefarina, Islam Md Asiful. (2021). Blood Transfusion Knowledge among Nurses in Malaysia: A University Hospital Experience. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph182111194
title: Modified Routine Blood Transfusion Knowledge Questionnaire (RBTKQ)
description: The RBTKQ is a 43-item questionnaire in seven sections used to assess nurses' blood transfusion knowledge, covering demographics and training, blood bag collection and patient preparation, pre- and post-transfusion nursing responsibilities, complications, and hospital policy. The article used a modified version with "a good reliability score of 68.3 based on the Flesch Reading Ease Index", a maximum score of 56 points, and scoring bands of <50%, 50–74%, and ≥75% for poor, moderate, and high knowledge.
requirements: Requires correct-response scoring with 1 point per item, 5 points for the multi-step patient identification item, and no points for conflicting responses
constraints: The authors note certain aspects of transfusion, such as signs and symptoms of AHTR like back or kidney pain, may have been overlooked by this questionnaire
target_learners: Registered nurses involved in blood transfusion procedures
target_learning_goals: Blood transfusion knowledge including patient preparation, pre- and post-transfusion responsibilities, complications, and policy
examples: Administered to 200 registered nurses at Hospital Universiti Sains Malaysia in a cross-sectional survey
key_sources: Mohd Noor Noor Haslina, Saad Noor Hafiza, Khan Mohammad, Hassan Mohd Nazri, Ramli Marini, Bahar Rosnah, Mohamed Yusoff Shafini, Iberahim Salfarina, Wan Ab Rahman Wan Suriana, Zulkafli Zefarina, Islam Md Asiful. (2021). Blood Transfusion Knowledge among Nurses in Malaysia: A University Hospital Experience. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph182111194

citation: McWilliam R. A., Boavida Tânia, Bull Kerry, Cañadas Margarita, Hwang Ai-Wen, Józefacka Natalia, Lim Hong Huay, Pedernera Marisú, Sergnese Tamara, Woodward Julia. (2020). The Routines-Based Model Internationally Implemented. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph17228308
title: RBI Plus: Routines-Based Interview with ecomap, participation-based child goals, and family goals
description: RBI Plus is the needs-assessment and intervention-planning package that all implementers adopted. It consists of the Routines-Based Interview accompanied by "an ecomap (depicting a family's informal, intermediate, and formal supports), participation-based goals for children, and family goals for siblings and parents." The RBI "is a needs assessment and typically results in 10–12 goals/outcomes," a long list of family-chosen goals the authors call one of the hallmarks of the model. Functional goals are written with criteria for acquisition, generalization, and maintenance.
requirements: An early interventionist trained to conduct the RBI with fidelity
constraints: In Portugal, mixing the RBM into a broader manual diluted the effect of the model
target_learners: Families of young children with disabilities in early intervention
target_learning_goals: Family-chosen functional goals for child participation in routines and family needs
examples: In one Singapore agency, the ecomap and RBI are the most widely adopted components of the RBM
key_sources: McWilliam R. A., Boavida Tânia, Bull Kerry, Cañadas Margarita, Hwang Ai-Wen, Józefacka Natalia, Lim Hong Huay, Pedernera Marisú, Sergnese Tamara, Woodward Julia. (2020). The Routines-Based Model Internationally Implemented. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph17228308

article_title: Resource Letter: RBAI-1: Research-based Assessment Instruments in Physics and Astronomy
citation: Adrian Madsen, Sam McKagan, and Eleanor C. Sayre. (2016). Resource Letter RBAI-1: Research-based Assessment Instruments in Physics and Astronomy. American Association of Physics Teachers, College Park, MD. https://physport.org/assessments
title: Taxonomy of physics and astronomy RBAIs organized by topic, research validation, instructional level, and format
description: The resource letter presents an organizing taxonomy of content RBAIs in physics and astronomy. It states: "In this resource letter, we present an overview of all content RBAIs in physics and astronomy by topic, research validation, instructional level, format, and themes, to help faculty find the best assessment for their course." The topic branches span mechanics, electricity and magnetism, quantum mechanics and modern physics, thermodynamics, waves and optics, and astronomy, from high school to graduate school.
requirements: Requires knowledge of the research validation categories, instructional level, and format of each instrument to apply the taxonomy as intended
constraints: The letter covers only content assessments; a second resource letter discusses non-content topics such as attitudes, epistemologies, problem solving, and lab skills
Statistical mechanics is the one major content area for which the authors are unaware of any research-based assessment
target_learners: physics and astronomy students from high school to graduate school
target_learning_goals: measuring conceptual understanding of physics and astronomy content
examples: Mechanics is treated as four sub-areas (kinematics and forces, energy, rotation, intermediate mechanics), with a table per sub-area
key_sources: Adrian Madsen, Sam McKagan, and Eleanor C. Sayre. (2016). Resource Letter RBAI-1: Research-based Assessment Instruments in Physics and Astronomy. American Association of Physics Teachers, College Park, MD. https://physport.org/assessments

article_title: Resource Letter: RBAI-1: Research-based Assessment Instruments in Physics and Astronomy
citation: Adrian Madsen, Sam McKagan, and Eleanor C. Sayre. (2016). Resource Letter RBAI-1: Research-based Assessment Instruments in Physics and Astronomy. American Association of Physics Teachers, College Park, MD. https://physport.org/assessments
title: Four-level research validation classification for assessment instruments: gold, silver, bronze, and research-based
description: The article defines a research validation classification based on how many of its seven research validation categories apply to an assessment. "RBAIs will have a gold level validation when they have been rigorously developed and recognized by a wider research community. Silver-level RBAIs are well-validated, but only by the developers and not the larger community." Bronze-level assessments have some validation but missing pieces, and research-based validation means an assessment is likely in early stages. The classification is grounded in "the steps to developing a good research-based assessment."
requirements: The seven categories of research validation listed in the article's Table II, derived from the development steps
constraints: Silver level may reflect an instrument being new rather than lower quality; the level depends on community recognition, not only on the validation work done
target_learners: physics and astronomy students at all instructional levels
target_learning_goals: judging the evidentiary quality of assessments of student learning
examples: The letter assigns each instrument in its per-topic tables a validation level so faculty can weigh the evidence base before adopting an assessment
key_sources: Adrian Madsen, Sam McKagan, and Eleanor C. Sayre. (2016). Resource Letter RBAI-1: Research-based Assessment Instruments in Physics and Astronomy. American Association of Physics Teachers, College Park, MD. https://physport.org/assessments
